dose: 100:40:40 NPK kg/ha, 50% N at sowing, 25% at tillering, 25% at jointing
dos: Sow between early November and mid-December for optimal tillering
Top-dress nitrogen only after a light irrigation for best uptake
Monitor yellow rust pustules on lower leaves during cool cloudy spells
donts: Do not delay first irrigation beyond 21 days after sowing (crown root stage)
Avoid late sowing past December — yield drops ~1.5% per delayed day

fertilizer: No heavy N now; foliar nutrition only if pale
dose: 2% urea foliar spray if crop looks pale
dos: Irrigate lightly at flowering to prevent grain sterility
Watch for aphids on ear heads — blast of water or neem first
donts: Never spray non-selective herbicides at flowering
Avoid deep irrigation that causes lodging in windy weather

dose: 120:60:40 NPK kg/ha + 25 kg zinc sulphate/ha, N in 3 splits
dos: Maintain 2-5 cm standing water for the first 2 weeks after transplanting
Drain field 10-14 days before harvest for uniform ripening
donts: Do not apply N blindly after panicle initiation — delays maturity
Avoid continuous flooding in direct-seeded rice — alternate wetting-drying saves 25% water

dos: Allow shallow drying for 2-3 days mid-tillering to boost root growth
Hand-weed between rows to cut competition for the N you apply
donts: Do not let cracks dry wider than a pencil — re-percolation wastes water

dose: 120:60:60 NPK kg/ha, 1/3 basal, 1/3 squaring, 1/3 boll development
dos: Scout pink bollworm pheromone traps weekly — 8 moths/trap/3 nights = action
Square retention above 60% means crop is on track
donts: Do not spray pyrethroids early season — they kill natural enemies and flare whitefly

dos: Pick bolls at 60-70% boll opening for best staple quality
Avoid moisture stress now — fiber length is decided in this window
donts: Do not use defoliants before 60% bolls open

dose: 20 t FYM/ha + 250:250:250 kg NPK/ha through splits, weekly fertigation preferred
dos: Stake plants and prune suckers for airflow — cuts fungal load dramatically
Use yellow sticky traps at canopy height to monitor whitefly and leaf miner
donts: Do not overhead-irrigate in the evening — late blight loves wet nights
Avoid harvesting wet fruit — shelf life halves

dos: Maintain even soil moisture to prevent blossom-end rot
Harvest at breaker stage for transport markets, full red for local sale
donts: Do not let soil crack between irrigations — fruit cracking follows

dose: 280:80:100 kg NPK/ha; N in 3 splits through tillering to grand growth
dos: Trash mulch between rows conserves ~20% soil moisture
Earthing-up at 90-100 days prevents lodging and improves ratoon yield
donts: Do not stop irrigation abruptly before harvest — sucrose % drops

dose: 120:60:40 kg NPK/ha; 50% N basal, 50% at knee-high stage
dos: Critical irrigation windows: knee-high and tasseling-silking — never miss these
Fall armyworm: look for ragged whorl feeding, act within 48 hours
donts: Do not delay harvest past black layer — grain loses test weight

dose: 25:50:25 NPK kg/ha + gypsum 250 kg/ha at pegging
dos: Apply gypsum at pegging — it directly fills pods with calcium
Harvest when 70-80% pods show dark veins inside the shell
donts: Do not over-water at pegging — pod rot follows

dose: 30:60:30 NPK kg/ha, SSP-based P with Rhizobium seed treatment
dos: Sow with first monsoon rains for proper germination
Inspect girdle beetle and semilooper weekly till pod fill
donts: Do not grow soybean after soybean — volunteer plants carry pests and diseases
